files.title: # Correction of assistant-authored instructions — 2026-10-23
first_25_lines: # Correction of assistant-authored instructions — 2026-10-23
This correction was requested by the user. The original record below is
preserved unchanged; the assistant's superseded interpretations are not current
requirements. No replacement scoring formula is adopted here.
The user's controlling instructions, verbatim:

> These individual scores need to be multipliers or sum in some way. WTF else would you do? Why do you keep trying to do somethign else. This is literally what I told you to do before with experimental reliablity
> THE PAPERS DO NOT OVERRIDE THE TEMPLATE. THEY GET CONVERTED THOUGHTFULLY
The papers supply measurements, experimental comparisons and limitations to
convert into the user's scoring template. They do not authorize replacing that
template with a new organization or with overall category grades. Individual
numerical components require their actual inputs and calculations, followed by
explicit sums/multipliers. Research examples must inform those calculations;
retaining measurements beside an overall grade does not accomplish this.
Specific corrections to assistant text in the preserved record:
- The five-level transfer scale is rejected, not still awaiting acceptance.
Evidence relevance still requires component calculations and combination;
the user did not restrict its evidence to sequence homology.
- The categorical experimental-relevance, measurement-validity and attribution

first_25_lines: # Resource episode direction: additive correction001
Record: `RESOURCE_EPISODE_CORRECTION_2026-10-22_001`.
This amendment withdraws the coordinator/root's incorrect resource diagnosis
and records the user's clarification. Earlier records, code, publications and
the fixed41 checklist remain unchanged. No implementation or access operation
is authorized by this document.
## Exact user clarification
These are verbatim excerpts supplied for this correction:
> API versus local execution is decided before launch is something I told you
> API vs local vs HPC are all different episodes. They are not adapters, they
> are fundamentally different episode structures and monitoring structures.
> HPC will likely require further sub-episodes to handle the actual
> environmental set up in addition to execution, so execution may be multi-step.
> Monitoring for HPC will differ as well b/c you will look at queue and priority
> scores.
> You will collect that information so that future runs can use it.

files.title: # Mandatory task/steering distinction, 2026-10-23
first_25_lines: # Mandatory task/steering distinction, 2026-10-23
This additive amendment applies to episode structure and information-library
construction. The historical EPISODE_STRUCTURE.md and TOOL_KNOWLEDGE.md are
read-only records and remain unchanged.
The full current requirement is in [TASK_AND_STEERING.md](../TASK_AND_STEERING.md)
and the mandatory section of [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md).
One decision prompt contains two different parts with opposite purposes and
verbosity:
- **TASK:** detailed instructional information defining the actual work and
problem-solving process. Supply it on every iteration. A goal heading or a
process/tool name is not a substitute for substantive instructions.
- **STEERING:** controlled, curt, dry factual information from prior iterations,
stripped to what affects the next decision and rendered in concise tables.
Selected information-library process instructions help construct TASK, including
the actual distinctions, alternatives and outcome contingencies. Prior outcomes,
attempts and yield/uncertainty tables supply STEERING. Do not apply steering's
compression policy to the task, or use task detail to justify expanding history.
Apply this distinction within every episode, in parent-to-child task construction,
and in child-to-parent steering returns. JSON is an internal intermediate for
